subthemes.name: Building stronger models for graph data
subthemes.gist: Papers developing new types of neural networks that learn better from graph-structured data by improving how information flows between connected nodes and capturing long-range relationships.

subthemes.name: Learning from the shape and structure of data
subthemes.gist: Papers that use geometric and topological ideas like symmetries, manifolds, and higher-dimensional shapes to help models understand data structure more deeply.

subthemes.name: Finding patterns and anomalies in networks
subthemes.gist: Papers focused on detecting unusual nodes or patterns in graphs, clustering similar items together, and understanding what makes certain nodes or subgraphs stand out.

subthemes.name: Generating and transforming graphs
subthemes.gist: Papers on creating new graphs or modifying existing ones using generative models and optimization techniques to solve graph-based problems.

subthemes.name: Understanding knowledge and relationships at scale
subthemes.gist: Papers that handle complex networks like knowledge graphs and databases, extracting meaning from relationships between entities and reasoning over connected information.

subthemes.name: Making graph models work in real conditions
subthemes.gist: Papers addressing practical challenges like handling missing data, domain shift, adversarial robustness, and personalizing models for different scenarios in graph learning.

subthemes.name: Learning representations and embeddings
subthemes.gist: Papers on extracting meaningful vector representations from graphs that capture structure and relationships, using techniques like contrastive learning and self-supervision.

subthemes.name: Connecting graphs to language and modern architectures
subthemes.gist: Papers that bridge graph learning with large language models and transformers, enabling graphs to work with text and taking advantage of modern deep learning frameworks.
